about.title: Dunsmuir Slip & Fall Claims
about.longDescription: Dunsmuir's small-town footprint, from the shops along Dunsmuir Avenue to properties near Castle Avenue and the I-5 corridor, means falls often happen on staircases, icy sidewalks, poorly lit parking areas, or uneven flooring inside local businesses. Siskiyou County's mountain climate adds wet leaves, snowmelt, and black ice to the list of hazards property owners are expected to manage. Under California law, an injured person generally has to show the property owner knew or reasonably should have known about the hazardous condition and failed to fix it or warn visitors. That's why documenting the scene, hazard, and any surveillance footage matters early. Our team can evaluate your Dunsmuir fall, explain your options, and work on contingency so you owe nothing unless you recover.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney About Your Fall

items.title: Notice Is Often the Key Issue
items.desc: California requires showing the property owner knew or should have known about the hazard. We can help gather evidence, like maintenance logs or prior complaints, that speaks to notice.

items.title: Surveillance Video Disappears Fast
items.desc: Many businesses overwrite security footage within days or weeks. Acting quickly to request preservation can matter for a Dunsmuir fall on private property.

items.title: Comparative Fault Doesn't Bar Your Claim
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, so even if you're partly responsible for a fall, you may still recover a reduced amount based on the property owner's share of fault.

items.question: How long do I have to file a slip-and-fall claim in Dunsmuir?
items.answer: California generally allows two years from the date of the injury to file a premises liability lawsuit. If the property involved is owned by a public entity, like a city or county building, the deadline is much shorter and requires an early claim. It's best to have us review the specifics of where the fall happened as soon as possible.

items.question: What if the fall happened at a business on Dunsmuir Avenue but I'm not sure who owns the property?
items.answer: That's a common situation, especially with older storefronts where ownership and management may be separate. We can help identify the responsible parties through public records and lease agreements. This is part of why documenting the location and getting photos matters right after the fall.

items.question: Does it cost anything to talk to an attorney?
items.answer: No. We offer free consultations, and we work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover compensation. There's no obligation to move forward after speaking with us.
